intro.en: It is lunch break. Your friends Kabir and Tanya have a plan, and they want you in on it.
intro.hg: Lunch break chal raha hai. Tumhare dost Kabir aur Tanya ne ek plan banaya hai, aur woh chahte hain ki tum bhi shamil ho.

text.en: Kabir says, 'Dare: write something funny about Arnav on the class board before the teacher comes. He's such a nerd.' Tanya is already giggling. You do not think it is funny.
text.hg: Kabir bolta hai, 'Dare: teacher ke aane se pehle class board par Arnav ke baare mein kuch funny likh de. Kitna nerd hai woh.' Tanya pehle se hans rahi hai. Tumhe yeh funny nahi lag raha.

label.en: Say, 'No, I'm not doing that. Let's play something else.'
label.hg: Bolo, 'Nahi, mujhe yeh nahi karna. Chalo kuch aur khelte hain.'

feedback.en: A short, firm no with another idea is hard to argue with. You protected Arnav and stayed in control without attacking your friends.
feedback.hg: Chhota, firm 'no' aur saath mein doosra idea, isse argue karna mushkil hai. Tumne Arnav ko protect kiya aur apne doston par attack kiye bina control apne haath mein rakha.

label.en: Say, 'My mum will be furious if I get a complaint.'
label.hg: Bolo, 'Complaint ghar gayi toh mummy bahut gussa hongi.'

feedback.en: Using a home rule as an excuse is a fair way out when a plain no feels hard. It works for today, though your friends still do not know you find the dare unkind.
feedback.hg: Jab seedha 'no' bolna mushkil lage, toh ghar ke rule ka excuse nikalne ka theek raasta hai. Aaj ke liye yeh kaam kar jayega, par tumhare doston ko ab bhi nahi pata ki tumhe yeh dare unkind lagta hai.

label.en: Write it quickly so they stop calling you boring.
label.hg: Jaldi se likh do taaki woh tumhe boring bolna band karein.

feedback.en: It is understandable to want to fit in. But Arnav gets hurt, you may get into trouble, and the next dare usually gets bigger. A calm no now is easier than undoing it later.
feedback.hg: Group mein fit hone ki chaah samajh mein aati hai. Par isse Arnav hurt hota hai, tum trouble mein pad sakte ho, aur agla dare aksar aur bada hota hai. Abhi calm 'no' bolna baad mein theek karne se easy hai.

text.en: Kabir rolls his eyes. 'You're so boring. Fine, Tanya will do it.' Tanya picks up the chalk and looks at you.
text.hg: Kabir aankhein ghumata hai. 'Kitne boring ho tum. Theek hai, Tanya kar degi.' Tanya chalk uthati hai aur tumhari taraf dekhti hai.

label.en: Say, 'Come on, leave him alone. It's not funny for him,' and walk towards the playground.
label.hg: Bolo, 'Chhodo na, use rehne do. Uske liye yeh funny nahi hai,' aur playground ki taraf chal do.

feedback.en: Speaking up once, calmly, often gives others permission to stop too. Walking away shows you mean it and removes the audience that the joke needs.
feedback.hg: Ek baar calmly bol dene se aksar doosron ko bhi rukne ki himmat mil jati hai. Wahan se chale jana dikhata hai ki tum seriously aisa maante ho, aur mazaak ko jo audience chahiye woh hat jati hai.

label.en: Stay quiet and walk away.
label.hg: Chup raho aur wahan se chale jao.

feedback.en: Leaving means you did not take part, and that matters. Arnav may still get hurt, though. Telling a teacher quietly afterwards is not snitching; it is looking out for a classmate.
feedback.hg: Chale jaane ka matlab hai ki tum isme shamil nahi hue, aur yeh matter karta hai. Par Arnav phir bhi hurt ho sakta hai. Baad mein quietly teacher ko batana chugli nahi hai; yeh ek classmate ka khayal rakhna hai.

label.en: Laugh along so Kabir stops calling you boring.
label.hg: Saath mein hans do taaki Kabir tumhe boring bolna band kare.

feedback.en: Laughing can feel safer than standing out. But to Arnav, the people laughing are part of the teasing. You can still fix it: stop, and check on him later.
feedback.hg: Alag dikhne se hans dena zyada safe lag sakta hai. Par Arnav ke liye hansne wale log bhi teasing ka hissa hain. Tum ab bhi ise fix kar sakte ho: ruk jao, aur baad mein uska haal poocho.

text.en: After lunch, Arnav is sitting alone at the back, looking upset. He knows your group was making fun of him.
text.hg: Lunch ke baad Arnav peeche akela baitha hai aur upset dikh raha hai. Use pata hai ki tumhara group uska mazaak uda raha tha.

label.en: Sit with him and say, 'That wasn't okay. Are you all right?'
label.hg: Uske paas baitho aur bolo, 'Jo hua woh theek nahi tha. Tum theek ho?'

feedback.en: Checking on someone who was targeted tells them they are not alone. If you joined in earlier, add a real sorry. Small acts like this are what good friends are made of.
feedback.hg: Jise target kiya gaya uska haal poochna use batata hai ki woh akela nahi hai. Agar tum pehle isme shamil the, toh ek real sorry bhi bolo. Aise chhote steps se hi achhe dost bante hain.

label.en: Say nothing to him now, but tell the class teacher what happened.
label.hg: Abhi usse kuch mat bolo, par class teacher ko bata do ki kya hua.

feedback.en: Involving a teacher is a responsible step, especially if the teasing keeps happening. A kind word to Arnav as well would mean a lot to him.
feedback.hg: Teacher ko involve karna responsible step hai, khaaskar agar teasing baar-baar ho rahi ho. Saath mein Arnav se do kind words bolna uske liye bahut matter karega.

debrief.en: Peer pressure works because nobody wants to be left out. A short, calm no, another suggestion and walking away are real skills, and they get easier with practice. Friends worth keeping may grumble, but they will not drop you for refusing to hurt someone.
debrief.hg: Peer pressure isliye kaam karta hai kyunki koi left out nahi hona chahta. Chhota, calm 'no', doosra idea aur wahan se chale jana real skills hain, aur practice se easy hote jate hain. Jo dost rakhne layak hain woh thoda badbada sakte hain, par kisi ko hurt karne se mana karne par tumhe drop nahi karenge.

intro.en: You have been dating Rehan, a classmate, for two months. Tonight his messages take a new turn.
intro.hg: Tum do mahine se apne classmate Rehan ko date kar rahe ho. Aaj raat uske messages ek naya turn lete hain.

text.en: Rehan texts: 'Send me your Insta password. Couples share everything. If you have nothing to hide, what's the problem?'
text.hg: Rehan text karta hai: 'Apna Insta password bhejo. Couples sab kuch share karte hain. Agar chhupane ko kuch nahi hai, toh problem kya hai?'

label.en: Reply: 'I like you, but my password stays with me. If something is worrying you, let's talk about it.'
label.hg: Reply karo: 'Tum mujhe pasand ho, par mera password mere paas rahega. Agar koi baat worry kar rahi hai, toh us par baat karte hain.'

feedback.en: You kept your boundary and still opened the door to a real conversation. Privacy is not secrecy, and a caring partner can hear this without punishing you.
feedback.hg: Tumne apni boundary banaye rakhi aur saath hi real conversation ka darwaza bhi khola. Privacy ka matlab secrecy nahi hai, aur care karne wala partner yeh baat tumhe punish kiye bina sun sakta hai.

label.en: Change the topic and hope he forgets.
label.hg: Topic change kar do aur hope karo ki woh bhool jayega.

feedback.en: Avoiding the question buys time, but the request will probably return. Saying your boundary once, clearly, is kinder to both of you than leaving it hanging.
feedback.hg: Question avoid karne se thoda time mil jata hai, par request shayad wapas aayegi. Apni boundary ek baar clearly bol dena, baat ko hanging chhodne se tum dono ke liye better hai.

label.en: Send the password to prove you trust him.
label.hg: Trust prove karne ke liye password bhej do.

feedback.en: Wanting to reassure someone you like is natural. But access given under pressure rarely stops at one request, and your account holds other people's private chats too. You can change the password and reset the boundary.
feedback.hg: Jo pasand hai use reassure karna chahna natural hai. Par pressure mein diya gaya access shayad hi ek request par rukta hai, aur tumhare account mein doosron ki private chats bhi hain. Tum password change karke boundary reset kar sakte ho.

text.en: Rehan replies: 'Wow. So you don't trust me.' Then he stops replying and leaves you on seen all evening.
text.hg: Rehan reply karta hai: 'Wow. Matlab tumhe mujh par trust nahi hai.' Phir woh reply karna band kar deta hai aur poori shaam tumhe seen par chhod deta hai.

label.en: Message once: 'I do trust you. Trust doesn't need my password. I'm here when you want to talk,' and then get on with your evening.
label.hg: Ek baar message karo: 'Mujhe tum par trust hai. Trust ke liye mera password zaroori nahi. Jab baat karna chaho, main yahin hoon,' aur phir apni evening mein lag jao.

feedback.en: You named the issue without begging or attacking. Silence used to make you give in is a pressure tactic; not chasing it shows that your boundary does not depend on his mood.
feedback.hg: Tumne beg ya attack kiye bina asli baat bol di. Tumse haan bulwane ke liye use ki gayi silence ek pressure tactic hai; uske peeche na bhaagna dikhata hai ki tumhari boundary uske mood par depend nahi karti.

label.en: Send ten messages apologising, without giving the password.
label.hg: Password diye bina sorry ke das messages bhej do.

feedback.en: It is hard to sit with someone's silence, so this is understandable. But repeated apologies teach both of you that your boundary is something to feel guilty about. One calm message is enough.
feedback.hg: Kisi ki silence jhelna mushkil hota hai, isliye yeh samajh mein aata hai. Par baar-baar sorry bolna tum dono ko yahi sikhata hai ki tumhari boundary koi galti hai jis par guilty feel karna chahiye. Ek calm message kaafi hai.

label.en: Give him the password so that he starts talking again.
label.hg: Password de do taaki woh phir se baat karne lage.

feedback.en: The silence hurts, and ending it feels urgent. But this shows that going quiet works, so it is likely to be used again. A boundary can be put back: change the password and say why.
feedback.hg: Silence chubhti hai, aur use khatam karna urgent lagta hai. Par isse yeh prove hota hai ki chup ho jana kaam karta hai, toh yeh tareeka dobara use ho sakta hai. Boundary wapas lagayi ja sakti hai: password change karo aur reason bata do.

text.en: The next day Rehan has a new request: 'Share your live location with me every evening. I just want to know you're safe.'
text.hg: Agle din Rehan ki ek nayi request hai: 'Har shaam apni live location mujhse share kiya karo. Main bas jaanna chahta hoon ki tum safe ho.'

label.en: Say, 'No. I'll tell you when I'm home if I want to. I'm noticing these requests keep growing, and I'm not okay with being tracked.'
label.hg: Bolo, 'Nahi. Mann hua toh ghar pahunch kar bata dunga/dungi. Main notice kar raha/rahi hoon ki yeh requests badhti ja rahi hain, aur track hona mujhe okay nahi hai.'

feedback.en: You spotted the pattern, not just the single request. One ask is not proof of anything, but requests that keep growing after each no deserve attention and a conversation with someone you trust.
feedback.hg: Tumne sirf ek request nahi, poora pattern dekha. Ek baar maangna kisi baat ka proof nahi hai, par har 'no' ke baad badhti jaane wali requests par dhyan dena aur kisi trusted insaan se baat karna zaroori hai.

label.en: Agree to share your location 'just for a week'.
label.hg: 'Bas ek hafte ke liye' location share karne ko maan jao.

feedback.en: Wanting peace makes sense. But this is a second demand in two days, and live location lets someone track where you are every evening. 'Just a week' often stretches. You can switch it off, say why, and talk to a friend or trusted adult about the pattern.
feedback.hg: Peace banaye rakhna chahna samajh mein aata hai. Par yeh do din mein doosri demand hai, aur live location se koi har shaam track kar sakta hai ki tum kahan ho. 'Bas ek hafta' aksar lamba khinch jata hai. Tum ise switch off kar sakte ho, reason bata sakte ho, aur is pattern ke baare mein kisi dost ya trusted adult se baat kar sakte ho.

debrief.en: Trust is shown by how someone treats your no, not by how much access you hand over. A single request is not a verdict on a person. A pattern of escalating demands, sulking or silence when refused is worth noticing early and discussing with a friend or trusted adult.
debrief.hg: Trust is baat se dikhta hai ki koi tumhari 'no' ke saath kaisa behave karta hai, isse nahi ki tumne kitna access de diya. Ek request kisi insaan par verdict nahi hai. Lekin badhti demands, mana karne par muh phulane ya silent ho jaane ka pattern jaldi notice karna aur kisi dost ya trusted adult se us par baat karna zaroori hai.

intro.en: Your close friend Ishita, 17, has been seeing Varun for three months. Lately she is hardly around.
intro.hg: Tumhari close dost Ishita, 17, teen mahine se Varun ke saath relationship mein hai. Aajkal woh mushkil se hi dikhti hai.

text.en: At first Varun sent Ishita gifts and messages all day. Now she has left your group chat and skips your plans. Today she whispers, 'Varun gets upset if I hang out without him. He says he just loves me too much.'
text.hg: Shuru mein Varun Ishita ko din bhar gifts aur messages bhejta tha. Ab Ishita ne tumhara group chat chhod diya hai aur tumhare plans skip karti hai. Aaj woh dheere se bolti hai, 'Main uske bina kahin jaun toh Varun upset ho jata hai. Bolta hai ki woh mujhse bas bahut zyada pyaar karta hai.'

label.en: Say, 'I've missed you. How do you feel about that rule?' and listen.
label.hg: Bolo, 'Tumhe bahut miss kiya. Is rule ke baare mein tumhe kaisa lagta hai?' aur uski baat suno.

feedback.en: An open question lets Ishita think aloud without feeling judged. People in controlling relationships are often told their friends are against them; listening first proves the opposite.
feedback.hg: Open question Ishita ko bina judge hue apni baat sochne aur bolne deta hai. Controlling relationships mein logon ko aksar bola jata hai ki unke dost unke against hain; pehle sunna iska ulta prove karta hai.

label.en: Say, 'That's a bit much, but it's your life,' and drop it.
label.hg: Bolo, 'Yeh thoda zyada hai, par life tumhari hai,' aur baat chhod do.

feedback.en: Respecting her choices matters, but dropping the subject can leave her alone with it. You can respect her decisions and still say gently that you are concerned.
feedback.hg: Uski choices ki respect karna zaroori hai, par baat chhod dene se woh iske saath akeli reh sakti hai. Tum uske decisions respect karte hue bhi gently bol sakte ho ki tumhe concern hai.

label.en: Say, 'He's toxic. Dump him or I'm done with you.'
label.hg: Bolo, 'Woh toxic hai. Use dump karo, warna main tumse done hoon.'

feedback.en: Your worry makes sense. But a label and an ultimatum usually push a friend to defend the partner and pull away from you, which leaves her more isolated. Staying connected helps her more.
feedback.hg: Tumhari worry sahi hai. Par label lagana aur ultimatum dena aksar dost ko partner ko defend karne aur tumse door hone ki taraf push karta hai, jisse woh aur isolated ho jati hai. Connected rehna uski zyada help karta hai.

text.en: A week later Ishita messages you late at night: 'He went through my phone and deleted some contacts. He was crying and saying he can't live without me. Maybe it's my fault for making him insecure.'
text.hg: Ek hafte baad Ishita late night tumhe message karti hai: 'Usne mera phone check kiya aur kuch contacts delete kar diye. Woh ro raha tha aur bol raha tha ki mere bina jee nahi sakta. Shayad galti meri hai ki main use insecure feel karati hoon.'

label.en: Reply: 'It's not your fault. Checking your phone and deleting contacts isn't okay. I'm worried, and I'm on your side whatever you decide.'
label.hg: Reply karo: 'Isme tumhari galti nahi hai. Phone check karna aur contacts delete karna okay nahi hai. Mujhe worry hai, aur tum jo bhi decide karo, main tumhari side hoon.'

feedback.en: You named the behaviour without attacking the person and lifted the blame off her. Hearing 'it is not your fault' from someone she trusts can cut through a lot of self-doubt.
feedback.hg: Tumne insaan par attack kiye bina behaviour ka naam liya aur Ishita ke sir se blame hataya. Kisi trusted insaan se 'isme tumhari galti nahi' sunna bahut saare self-doubt ko kaat sakta hai.

label.en: Reply: 'Every couple has problems. Just avoid making him jealous.'
label.hg: Reply karo: 'Har couple mein problems hoti hain. Bas use jealous mat hone do.'

feedback.en: You were trying to comfort her. But this tells her his behaviour is her job to manage, which is the blame she already feels. Going through her phone and deleting contacts is control, not an ordinary couple problem. Better: 'It's not your fault, and I'm worried about you.'
feedback.hg: Tum use comfort karna chah rahe the. Par isse use lagega ki Varun ke behaviour ko manage karna uska kaam hai, aur woh pehle se khud ko blame kar rahi hai. Phone check karna aur contacts delete karna control hai, koi normal couple problem nahi. Better reply: 'Isme tumhari galti nahi hai, aur mujhe tumhari worry hai.'

label.en: Screenshot her message and send it to your whole friend group.
label.hg: Uske message ka screenshot le kar poore friend group ko bhej do.

feedback.en: Wanting backup is understandable. But sharing her private message breaks her trust and could reach Varun, making things harder for her. Ask her first, or take it to one trusted adult instead.
feedback.hg: Backup chahna samajh mein aata hai. Par uska private message share karna uska trust todta hai, aur baat Varun tak pahunch sakti hai, jisse uski mushkil badhegi. Pehle usse poocho, ya ise kisi ek trusted adult tak le jao.

text.en: Ishita says, 'Please don't tell anyone. But I'm scared of how he'll react if I end it.'
text.hg: Ishita bolti hai, 'Please kisi ko mat batana. Par mujhe darr hai ki agar maine end kiya toh woh kaise react karega.'

label.en: Say, 'I won't spread it around, but I can't keep this just between us if you're scared. Let's talk to your sister or the school counsellor together, or call 1098.'
label.hg: Bolo, 'Main yeh baat failaunga/failaungi nahi, par agar tum dari hui ho toh ise sirf hum dono ke beech nahi rakh sakta/sakti. Chalo saath mein tumhari didi ya school counsellor se baat karte hain, ya 1098 par call karte hain.'

feedback.en: Fear of a partner's reaction is a safety issue, too big for two teenagers to carry alone. Being honest that you will involve one trusted adult, and offering to go with her, protects both her and the friendship.
feedback.hg: Partner ke reaction se darr lagna safety issue hai, itna bada ki do teenagers akele nahi utha sakte. Honestly batana ki tum ek trusted adult ko involve karoge, aur saath chalne ka offer dena, Ishita aur tumhari dosti dono ko protect karta hai.

label.en: Promise to keep it secret and check on her every day.
label.hg: Promise karo ki baat secret rakhoge aur roz uska haal poochoge.

feedback.en: Checking in daily is caring. But she has said she is scared of him, and a promise of secrecy leaves you both alone with that fear. Say you won't spread it, but you will involve one trusted adult, and offer to go with her or call 1098 together.
feedback.hg: Roz haal poochna caring hai. Par woh bol chuki hai ki use Varun se darr lagta hai, aur secret rakhne ka promise tum dono ko us darr ke saath akela chhod deta hai. Bolo ki tum baat failaoge nahi, par ek trusted adult ko involve karoge, aur uske saath chalne ya milkar 1098 par call karne ka offer do.

label.en: Message Varun yourself and warn him to back off.
label.hg: Khud Varun ko message karke warn karo ki peeche hat jaye.

feedback.en: Wanting to protect her is a good instinct. But confronting him can raise the risk for Ishita and for you. Safer support goes through her and a trusted adult, or Child Helpline 1098.
feedback.hg: Use protect karne ki chaah achhi instinct hai. Par Varun ko confront karne se Ishita aur tumhare liye risk badh sakta hai. Zyada safe support Ishita aur kisi trusted adult ke through, ya Child Helpline 1098 se milta hai.

debrief.en: One jealous comment does not define a relationship. What you saw here is a pattern: intense attention, then isolation, phone checking and fear. You cannot rescue a friend, but you can stay close, avoid blame, name the behaviour and help her reach a trusted adult or 1098. If anyone is in immediate danger, call 112.
debrief.hg: Ek jealous comment se koi relationship define nahi hota. Yahan tumne jo dekha woh ek pattern hai: pehle intense attention, phir isolation, phone checking aur darr. Tum dost ko rescue nahi kar sakte, par close reh sakte ho, blame se bach sakte ho, behaviour ka naam le sakte ho aur use kisi trusted adult ya 1098 tak pahunchne mein help kar sakte ho. Agar koi immediate danger mein ho, toh 112 par call karo.

intro.en: You are 26 and engaged to Kiran. The wedding is four months away, and you both work full-time in different cities.
intro.hg: Tum 26 ke ho aur Kiran se tumhari engagement ho chuki hai. Shaadi chaar mahine door hai, aur tum dono alag-alag cities mein full-time job karte ho.

text.en: At dinner with both families, Kiran says, 'After the wedding we'll live in Pune, obviously. You can find something there. One of us has to adjust.' Nobody has asked you. You love your job in Bengaluru.
text.hg: Dono families ke saath dinner par Kiran bolta hai, 'Shaadi ke baad hum Pune mein rahenge, obviously. Tumhe wahan kuch na kuch mil jayega. Kisi ek ko toh adjust karna padega.' Tumse kisi ne poocha nahi. Tumhe Bengaluru ki apni job bahut pasand hai.

label.en: Later, in private, say: 'I felt sidelined when the move was announced as decided. I want us to work this out together.'
label.hg: Baad mein privately bolo: 'Jab move ko decided maan kar announce kar diya gaya, toh mujhe sidelined feel hua. Main chahta/chahti hoon ki yeh hum milkar decide karein.'

feedback.en: Raising it privately, with one clear issue and your own feeling, gives Kiran a fair chance to respond. Big decisions announced by one person are worth questioning early, before they become the norm.
feedback.hg: Ise privately, ek clear issue aur apni feeling ke saath uthana Kiran ko respond karne ka fair chance deta hai. Jo bade decisions ek insaan announce kar de, un par shuru mein hi question karna sahi hai, isse pehle ki yeh norm ban jaye.

label.en: Say nothing tonight and plan to bring it up after the wedding shopping is done.
label.hg: Aaj raat kuch mat bolo aur socho ki shaadi ki shopping ke baad baat uthaoge.

feedback.en: Avoiding a scene at a family dinner is sensible. Postponing for weeks, though, lets everyone treat the move as settled. A calm conversation within a day or two keeps the question open.
feedback.hg: Family dinner par scene na banana samajhdari hai. Par hafton tak postpone karne se sab log move ko settled maan lenge. Ek-do din ke andar calm conversation kar lene se question open rehta hai.

label.en: Snap at the table: 'Nobody asked me! Maybe there shouldn't be a wedding.'
label.hg: Table par hi bhadak jao: 'Mujhse kisi ne poocha tak nahi! Shayad yeh shaadi honi hi nahi chahiye.'

feedback.en: The anger is fair; being left out of a decision about your own life hurts. But a threat in front of both families makes people take sides. The same point lands better in private.
feedback.hg: Gussa fair hai; apni hi life ke decision se bahar rakha jana hurt karta hai. Par dono families ke saamne di gayi dhamki logon ko sides lene par majboor karti hai. Yahi baat privately better land karti hai.

text.en: When you talk, Kiran sighs: 'You're overreacting. Everyone adjusts after marriage. My parents expect us to be nearby.'
text.hg: Jab tum baat karte ho, Kiran sigh karke bolta hai: 'Tum overreact kar rahe ho. Shaadi ke baad sab adjust karte hain. Mere parents expect karte hain ki hum paas rahein.'

label.en: Say: 'I hear that being near your parents matters to you. My work matters to me too. Can we list the options: Pune, Bengaluru, a transfer, or a year apart?'
label.hg: Bolo: 'Main samajh raha/rahi hoon ki parents ke paas rehna tumhare liye important hai. Mera kaam bhi mere liye important hai. Kya hum options list kar sakte hain: Pune, Bengaluru, transfer, ya ek saal alag-alag?'

feedback.en: You repeated back Kiran's concern, stated yours as equally real and moved to options. That shifts the talk from who wins to what could work for both.
feedback.hg: Tumne Kiran ki concern repeat ki, apni concern ko utna hi real bataya aur options ki taraf badhe. Isse baat 'kaun jeetega' se hat kar 'dono ke liye kya work kar sakta hai' par aa jati hai.

label.en: Say: 'Fine, I'll think about it,' and leave it there.
label.hg: Bolo: 'Theek hai, main sochunga/sochungi,' aur baat wahin chhod do.

feedback.en: Taking time to think is reasonable. Make sure it does not quietly turn into agreement. Name a day to continue the talk so that the decision stays shared.
feedback.hg: Sochne ke liye time lena theek hai. Bas dhyan rakho ki yeh chupchap agreement mein na badal jaye. Baat continue karne ka ek din fix kar lo taaki decision shared rahe.

label.en: Ask your parents to call Kiran's parents and push back.
label.hg: Apne parents se bolo ki Kiran ke parents ko call karke push back karein.

feedback.en: Wanting support is natural, and families often get involved. But sending parents to negotiate takes the decision away from the two people who must live with it. Talk directly first.
feedback.hg: Support chahna natural hai, aur families aksar involve ho hi jati hain. Par parents ko negotiate karne bhejne se decision un do logon ke haath se nikal jata hai jinhe uske saath jeena hai. Pehle directly baat karo.

text.en: A few days later Kiran says, 'I was unfair. I assumed. Can we sit down this weekend and talk about jobs, money and where we live, properly?'
text.hg: Kuch din baad Kiran bolta hai, 'Main unfair tha. Maine assume kar liya tha. Kya hum is weekend baith kar jobs, paise aur kahan rehna hai, is par properly baat kar sakte hain?'

label.en: Agree, and suggest that each of you writes down your priorities first so that nothing stays assumed.
label.hg: Maan jao, aur suggest karo ki pehle dono apni-apni priorities likh lein taaki kuch bhi assumed na rahe.

feedback.en: Writing priorities separately brings hidden expectations into the open. Couples who discuss work, money and family roles before marriage have fewer surprises to fight about later.
feedback.hg: Alag-alag priorities likhne se hidden expectations saamne aa jati hain. Jo couples shaadi se pehle kaam, paise aur family roles par baat kar lete hain, unke paas baad mein ladne layak surprises kam bachte hain.

label.en: Say, 'It's okay, forget it. I'll manage in Pune.'
label.hg: Bolo, 'Koi baat nahi, chhodo. Main Pune mein manage kar lunga/lungi.'

feedback.en: Kiran's apology is a good sign, and generosity is fine. But giving up something important just to end the tension can turn into resentment. Take the offered conversation; you may still choose Pune, freely.
feedback.hg: Kiran ki apology achha sign hai, aur generous hona theek hai. Par sirf tension khatam karne ke liye koi important cheez chhod dena aage chal kar resentment ban sakta hai. Jo conversation offer hui hai use accept karo; uske baad bhi tum apni marzi se Pune choose kar sakte ho.

debrief.en: Unspoken assumptions about careers, money and family are a common source of conflict. Fair conflict means raising one issue privately, describing your feeling, hearing the other side and looking for options together. A partner who can say 'I assumed, let's talk' is showing a healthy pattern; one who repeatedly dismisses you is showing a different one.
debrief.hg: Career, paise aur family ko lekar unspoken assumptions conflict ki common wajah hain. Fair conflict ka matlab hai ek issue privately uthana, apni feeling batana, saamne wale ki baat sunna aur milkar options dhoondhna. Jo partner bol sake 'maine assume kar liya tha, chalo baat karte hain', woh healthy pattern dikha raha hai; jo baar-baar tumhe dismiss kare, woh ek alag pattern dikha raha hai.

intro.en: You finally told Aanya, a friend from tuition, that you like her. Her answer was not the one you hoped for.
intro.hg: Finally tumne tuition ki apni dost Aanya ko bata diya ki tum use pasand karte ho. Uska jawab woh nahi tha jiski tumhe hope thi.

text.en: Aanya says, 'I'm really sorry. I like you as a friend, but I don't feel that way.' Your face feels hot and your stomach drops.
text.hg: Aanya bolti hai, 'I'm really sorry. Tum mujhe dost ki tarah achhe lagte ho, par mere mann mein waisa kuch nahi hai.' Tumhara chehra garam ho jata hai aur pet mein kuch doob-sa jata hai.

label.en: Say, 'Okay. Thanks for being honest,' and head home.
label.hg: Bolo, 'Okay. Honest hone ke liye thanks,' aur ghar chale jao.

feedback.en: That took courage. A short, calm reply respects her answer and keeps your dignity. The sting is real, and it is fine to go and feel it somewhere private.
feedback.hg: Isme courage laga. Chhota, calm reply uske answer ki respect karta hai aur tumhari dignity banaye rakhta hai. Chubhan real hai, aur kisi private jagah jaa kar use feel karna bilkul theek hai.

label.en: Say, 'I was just joking anyway,' and laugh.
label.hg: Bolo, 'Main toh bas mazaak kar raha tha/rahi thi,' aur hans do.

feedback.en: Covering up to save face is very human. It does blur an honest moment, though. You do not need to hide your feelings; having them is not embarrassing, and she already treated them kindly.
feedback.hg: Face save karne ke liye baat cover kar dena bahut human hai. Par isse ek honest moment blur ho jata hai. Tumhe apni feelings chhupane ki zaroorat nahi; unka hona embarrassing nahi hai, aur Aanya ne toh unhe kindly hi liya.

label.en: Ask, 'Why not? Just give me one chance. What's wrong with me?'
label.hg: Poocho, 'Kyun nahi? Bas ek chance do. Mujhme kya kami hai?'

feedback.en: Wanting an explanation is natural when you are hurt. But pushing for reasons or a 'chance' puts pressure on her after a clear no. Her answer is about her feelings, not a list of your faults.
feedback.hg: Hurt hone par explanation chahna natural hai. Par reasons ya 'ek chance' ke liye push karna clear 'no' ke baad us par pressure daalta hai. Uska answer uski feelings ke baare mein hai, tumhari kamiyon ki koi list nahi.

text.en: That evening your friend Dhruv says, 'Arre, a no is never final. Keep texting her, send gifts, she'll come around. That's how it works in every film.'
text.hg: Us shaam tumhara dost Dhruv bolta hai, 'Arre, no kabhi final nahi hoti. Text karte raho, gifts bhejo, maan jayegi. Har film mein aisa hi hota hai.'

label.en: Say, 'No. She gave me a clear answer and I'm going to respect it.'
label.hg: Bolo, 'Nahi. Usne mujhe clear answer diya hai aur main use respect karunga/karungi.'

feedback.en: Exactly right. Films make chasing look romantic, but in real life repeated contact after a no feels frightening and is harassment. Respecting her answer also frees you to move on.
feedback.hg: Bilkul sahi. Filmein chase karne ko romantic dikhati hain, par real life mein 'no' ke baad baar-baar contact karna darawna lagta hai aur harassment hai. Uske answer ki respect karna tumhe bhi move on karne ke liye free karta hai.

label.en: Do not text her, but check her profile and stories several times a day.
label.hg: Use text mat karo, par din mein kai baar uski profile aur stories check karte raho.

feedback.en: You are respecting her space, which matters. Constant checking keeps the hurt fresh, though. Muting her updates for a few weeks is not rude; it gives your mind a rest.
feedback.hg: Tum uske space ki respect kar rahe ho, aur yeh matter karta hai. Par baar-baar check karne se hurt fresh bana rehta hai. Kuch hafton ke liye uske updates mute kar dena rude nahi hai; isse tumhare mind ko rest milta hai.

label.en: Take the advice and send her messages every day for a week.
label.hg: Advice maan lo aur ek hafte tak roz use messages bhejo.

feedback.en: Hope can make this advice sound reasonable. But daily messages after a clear no will make her uncomfortable or scared, and can count as harassment. Stopping now and giving space is the respectful repair.
feedback.hg: Hope ki wajah se yeh advice theek lag sakti hai. Par clear 'no' ke baad roz ke messages use uncomfortable ya scared karenge, aur yeh harassment maana ja sakta hai. Abhi ruk jana aur use space dena hi respectful repair hai.

text.en: A week later you still feel low. A thought keeps coming back: 'Nobody will ever like me.'
text.hg: Ek hafte baad bhi tum low feel kar rahe ho. Ek thought baar-baar wapas aata hai: 'Mujhe kabhi koi pasand nahi karega.'

label.en: Tell a friend, sibling or parent how you feel, and get back to football practice and the things you enjoy.
label.hg: Kisi dost, sibling ya parent ko batao ki kaisa lag raha hai, aur football practice aur apni pasand ki cheezon mein wapas lag jao.

feedback.en: Talking shrinks the thought, and routine reminds you that your life is bigger than one answer. One person not feeling the same way says nothing about your worth.
feedback.hg: Baat karne se woh thought chhota pad jata hai, aur routine yaad dilata hai ki tumhari life ek answer se kahin badi hai. Ek insaan ke mann mein waisi feeling na hona tumhari worth ke baare mein kuch nahi batata.

label.en: Keep it to yourself and wait for it to pass.
label.hg: Baat apne tak rakho aur iske guzar jaane ka wait karo.

feedback.en: It often does pass with time. But carrying it alone makes it heavier than it needs to be. If the low mood lasts beyond two weeks, talk to someone you trust or call Tele-MANAS on 14416.
feedback.hg: Time ke saath yeh aksar guzar bhi jata hai. Par akele carry karne se bojh zaroorat se zyada heavy ho jata hai. Agar low mood do hafte se zyada rahe, toh kisi trusted insaan se baat karo ya Tele-MANAS 14416 par call karo.

debrief.en: Rejection hurts, and handling it well is a skill. Accept the first no, give the person space, ignore advice to 'keep trying', and look after yourself with people and routines you trust. A no tells you about one person's feelings. It is never a measurement of your worth.
debrief.hg: Rejection chubhta hai, aur use achhe se handle karna ek skill hai. Pehli 'no' accept karo, us insaan ko space do, 'try karte raho' wali advice ignore karo, aur trusted logon aur routine ke sahare apna khayal rakho. 'No' ek insaan ki feelings ke baare mein batati hai. Yeh kabhi tumhari worth ka measurement nahi hai.
